card.name: Words before growth-factor and antibody terms
card.fires_on: The word "anti" before a hyphenated target such as -D or -CD20 or -C5, and the middle of "granulocyte" before colony-stimulating factor. It also fires on linking words like "receiving" or "with" just before a therapy name.

modes.label: Anti- before a target
modes.description: The prefix "anti" or "Anti" starts a hyphenated antibody or immunoglobulin name.
modes.example: intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and<< anti>>-D immunoglobulin [see Clinical Studies

modes.label: Inside granulocyte
modes.description: The "ocyte" part of granulocyte, leading into colony-stimulating factor.
modes.example: Primary prophylaxis with granul<<ocyte>> colony-stimulating factor (G-CS

modes.label: Linking word before a therapy
modes.description: A word like receiving, with or a that links a patient or drug to a treatment or factor.
modes.example: sickle cell disorders<< receiving>> filgrastim products. Discontinue

card.writes: It seems to push toward word starts like "integr" and "posit", with no clear meaning for the suppressed tokens.
